newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken says H1 saw margin pressure.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken says H1 saw margin pressure.

text.p: Sweden's state controlled bank, Nordbanken, on Thursday posted a 21 percent fall in operating profit for the first half of 1997 which it said was marked by continuing pressure on interest rate margins.
Nordbanken reported an operating profit of 3.02 billion crowns, largely in line with market expectations of 3.08 billion crowns.
Loan losses fell to 194 million crowns from 260 million in the corresponding year-earlier period, while analysts had expected them to be largely unchanged at 254 million.
The fall in profit derived from a strong first half of 1996 which was partly lifted by sharply falling interest rates that boosted the bank's bond portfolio, the bank said in a statement.
Net interest income fell by seven percent to 4.92 billion crowns, hurt by lower interest rate margins and a higher fee for the government's bank guarantee.
"Higher volumes could not fully compensate for lower margins," the bank said.

Net commission income rose to 25 percent of net interest income from 19 percent in the year-earlier period. It rose 20 percent to 1.22 billion crowns, mainly on the back of increased income from fund and securities operations.
Net financial income dropped to 35 million crowns from 685 million.
Net financial income swung to a positive result of 163 million crowns in the second quarter from a loss of 128 million crowns in the first quarter, lifted by lower interest rates.
Operating costs rose three percent to 3.30 billion crowns, largely on higher information technology (IT) costs in the second quarter
The capital adequacy ratio rose to 12.4 percent in June from 11.8 percent in December 1996.
Private lending rose three percent in the first half of the year.
"Within the private market strong growth for mortgage volumes continued," Nordbanken said.
"During the second quarter the bank took about half of the market growth and credit volumes rose to 62 billion crowns."
Over the past 12 months, Nordbanken's market share rose by 1.5 percentage points to 12.4 percent.
Individuals kept saving more through funds and assets under management rose to 108 billion crowns at the end of June, the bank said without giving a comparison figure.
Nordbanken's share fell on the report, changing hands at 267 crowns at 1110 GMT, down three while the Stockholm Stock Exchange's general index was down 0.47 percent at 3,192.18.
